subject: Request: tiered cash holdback + buyout trigger schedule
messages:
From: Kris Miller <kris.miller@heliumhealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@heliumhealth.com
Date: 2025-10-19T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial ask — holdback + buyout language for SLA breaches

Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to follow up with a concrete ask on remedies for repeat P1/P2 latency incidents. Our security and risk teams are uncomfortable with credits alone. They want: a tiered cash holdback (1–3% of monthly committed spend held in escrow) that increases after each repeat P1 in a 90-day window, plus a defined buyout right if three P1s occur within 6 months.

We attached the draft exhibit the legal team prefers (see SLA-exhibit-proposal.xlsx). Our goal is to keep the commercial relationship simple but with a clear safety net if performance degrades repeatedly. Can Redwood confirm whether you can accept holdback + buyout language, and if so what minimum cure periods you need?

Kris
Kris Miller
Head of Procurement — Helium Health
From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: Kris Miller <kris.miller@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-19T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — holdback + buyout language for SLA breaches

Kris —

Thanks for the clear ask and for the XLSX. I ran this past Ben (sales ops) and Marissa (legal) for an initial reaction. Short answer: we understand the request and are open to a tiered cash holdback approach paired with a buyout/right-to-terminate, but we need to align on thresholds, cure windows, and whether the holdback accrues against future invoices or is escrowed.

Can you confirm the exact committed monthly spend the holdback percentage would apply to? Also, would Helium expect the holdback to be refundable pro rata on renewal/termination? That will affect the wording. Ben — can you pull the committed spend figure from the deal record and confirm whether a monthly escrow is feasible under our finance process? Marissa — please flag must-not-accept clauses (e.g., uncapped liquidated damages).

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-19T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — holdback + buyout language for SLA breaches

Quick finance note — deal record shows Helium is targeting $120k/mo committed for Year 1 (see HubSpot link). A 3% monthly holdback on committed spend would be $3.6k/month. We can route a retained amount to an escrow account if legal signs off, but it needs a clear release schedule. From an ops perspective, monthly escrow is doable; larger issue is whether the holdback is additive to credits or offsets them.

If Helium wants the holdback to be a separate cash safety net (not simply a pre-funded credit), we should specify that credits do not reduce the holdback pool unless both parties agree.

Ben Carter
Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-20T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — holdback + buyout language for SLA breaches

High-level legal guidance: we cannot accept uncapped liquidated damages. We can entertain a structured, capped buyout/termination payment based on remaining committed value (example: pro rata remaining term, capped at 12 months of committed spend) tied to a defined severity/occurrence ladder. Required items:

- Cure windows: 30 days for P2s, 14 days for P1s (or faster operational SLAs depending on incident)
- Clear definitions: what exactly constitutes a repeat P1 (same incident vs distinct root cause)
- Offset rules: whether credits reduce the escrow; recommend escrow remain separate but allow credit offsets for the incident that triggered the escrow release if explicitly agreed
- Escrow mechanics: third-party escrow agent or trust account; release on mutual written agreement or arbitration outcome

I recommend we propose a 3-tier model: 1% holdback after first P1 in 90 days, 2% after second P1 in 90 days, 3% after third P1; buyout right only after 3 P1s in a rolling 6-month period, with buyout capped at 12x monthly committed spend. We should also propose an initial cure/remediation plan requirement before buyout is exercised.

Marissa Cole
Director, Legal — Redwood Inference
From: Kris Miller <kris.miller@heliumhealth.com>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@heliumhealth.com
Date: 2025-10-21T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — holdback + buyout language for SLA breaches

Jordan & team —

Thanks, that framework is helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: Helium wants the holdback to accumulate in escrow and be unrelated to system credits (we view credits as operational remediation). The buyout cap at 12 months is acceptable; however, Risk insists on a shorter cure window for P1s (7 days) given patient-impacting workflows. They also want a definition that repeat P1 means distinct root-cause incidents affecting the service, not repeated alerts from the same incident after it was declared resolved.

We can accept arbitration for disputes about escrow release but would prefer a named escrow agent (we can share a shortlist). Next steps: would Redwood draft proposed SLA exhibit wording reflecting the 3-tier holdback and the 3-strike buyout with the 7-day P1 cure? If you can send a marked-up exhibit we will route to our general counsel.

Kris
From: jordan.blake@redwood.com
To: Kris Miller <kris.miller@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial ask — holdback + buyout language for SLA breaches

Kris —

Appreciate the clarity. We'll take the required changes and produce a marked-up SLA exhibit. Action plan: 1) Legal (Marissa) to draft exhibit with: 3-tier escrow percentages (1/2/3%), 7-day P1 cure, explicit repeat-P1 definition, buyout trigger after 3 distinct P1s in rolling 6 months, buyout cap = min(12 months committed, remaining term liability) and arbitration clause for escrow disputes; 2) Finance (Ben) to outline escrow mechanics and ledger treatment; 3) Solutions/CS (Monica) to suggest operational incident timelines that tie into the cure language. Expect a draft by COB 2025-10-24.

If Helium can confirm the escrow agent shortlist (or allow Redwood to propose one), that will speed the process.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
